name: @chanmeng666/archlang-mcp

tools.name: compile
tools.description: Compile ArchLang `.arch` source (or a Plan-JSON object) to an SVG floor plan, or with `format` to a plain-text ASCII plan ("txt"), Plan JSON ("json") or an image ("png"). Format "json" returns the plan as an object, with `schema` naming its JSON Schema; passed back as `plan_json` it compiles to the same drawing, unless the plan uses a part of the language Plan JSON does not carry (the sheet, styles, curves, roofs, storeys, `place`, accessibility metadata). Returns the output plus diagnostics; a diagnostic usually carries a byte span with line/col and an E_/W_ code, and often a fix, sometimes one the `fix` tool can apply. Errors come back as data, never as exceptions: read `diagnostics` and correct the source. A multi-storey plan (`level <n> { … }`) returns the lowest storey in `output` and every storey in `pages[]` ({ level, name, output }); pass `level` to render just one. format "png" returns the usual result as text, then the drawing (the lowest storey, or `level`) as image content, as wide as `width` says; it needs the optional renderer @resvg/resvg-js, and without it the call returns ok:false with an error saying how to install it.

source.description: ArchLang source (a `plan "…" { … }`). Provide this OR plan_json.

plan_json.description: Plan JSON (RPLAN shape) as an alternative to `source`; converted to .arch then compiled.

format.description: svg (default), txt (zero-dependency ASCII), json (Plan JSON, the shape `plan_json` takes) or png (an image; needs the optional renderer).

overlay.description: Draw an opt-in circulation overlay (SVG only).

level.description: Render only this storey of a multi-storey plan. An undeclared level is an error, not a guess.

width.description: png only (any other format refuses it): the image width in pixels, clamped to 256-4096, and narrower for a tall plan so neither side exceeds 4096; default 1600.

tools.name: describe
tools.description: Report a plan's facts without rendering, so you can check it against the brief without looking at an image. Returns rooms (area, bbox, adjacency, use, and the exact shape: `floor_polygon` for a `room polygon`, `floor_circle` for a `room circle`, whose area is exactly πR²), doors (what each connects), windows, circulation (walk distance, bottleneck width, detour), zones, storeys (`levels[i]` carries the same facts per floor) with the shafts that join them and which storeys stay reachable (`vertical`), the drawing extent (`bbox`, `bbox_outer`), `freedom` (which positions are hand-authored and which are derived), and totals.

tools.name: lint
tools.description: List advisory architectural-soundness warnings (`W_*` codes) as data: unreachable room, windowless bedroom, too-narrow door, blocked doorway, furniture through a wall, circuitous path, and more. `profile` selects a ruleset ("residential-basic", "accessibility-advisory", …).

profile.description: Advisory ruleset name (default: the built-in ruleset).

tools.name: validate
tools.description: Check a plan in one pass without returning a drawing (parse, resolve and lint): the gate a plan passes before it ships. `strict:true` makes advisory warnings fail too. Optional `graph` checks the plan's interior-door adjacency against an intended room graph (`{ room: [neighbours] }`); a mismatch fails. Optional `intent` (a brief's expectations, shaped as the `archlang://intent-schema` resource describes) is checked against the plan: a missed gating assertion (room count, existence, area, total area, windows) fails, while adjacency and reachability are advisory and only score. A malformed intent returns `{ ok:false, intentErrors }` as data, never an exception. Returns { ok, diagnostics, graph?, intent? }.

intent.description: A brief's intent JSON (shape: the archlang://intent-schema resource); gating assertions fail.

tools.name: score
tools.description: Measure how much of a brief's intent JSON a plan satisfies, without gating. Returns { ok, satisfied, total, score, subscores, violations }, where `score` is satisfied/total in [0,1] (an empty intent scores 1); call it across edits to watch a plan approach the brief. The intent's shape is the `archlang://intent-schema` resource. A malformed intent returns `{ ok:false, intentErrors }` as data, never an exception.

brief.description: A brief's intent JSON (shape: the archlang://intent-schema resource) to measure against.

tools.name: repair
tools.description: Correct furniture placement and return the corrected `.arch` source with a change log. It pushes furniture out of walls, doorways and door swings, separates overlapping pieces, moves fixtures that sit in the wrong room, and snaps floating pieces to walls. A piece it may not rewrite is listed in `unresolved` with the reason. It never adds doors or windows (that is a design choice); use `suggest` for those.

tools.name: fix
tools.description: Apply the machine-applicable fixes attached to a plan's compile diagnostics and return the edited source. It corrects source-level faults (an opening off its wall becomes the attachment form, an out-of-range position is clamped, …); furniture geometry is `repair`'s job. It runs at most 4 passes and rolls back a pass that raises the error count. `unsafe:true` also applies `maybe-incorrect` fixes. Returns { ok, passes, applied, skipped, source }.

tools.name: finish
tools.description: Complete a plan for export by adding what it lacks; run it once `lint` is clean. Two stages. `furnish` puts furniture, by room use, in each rectangular room that holds none (single-storey plans; a furnished room is never touched, and one that lacks a piece its use requires is named in `unresolved` with the missing pieces, not filled; placement is `against wall` / `in <room> anchor`, never absolute). `sheet` adds the sheet statements the plan lacks (`paper`, `scale`, `dims auto`, `title`, `schedule rooms`, `legend`), choosing the finest standard scale on the smallest sheet that holds the drawing. It fills only what is missing and deletes nothing; `only` runs one stage; `reissue:true` may replace `paper`/`scale` (only those) when the drawing does not fit them. Returns { ok, changed, changes, unresolved, source }; a plan that does not compile comes back untouched with `ok:false`, and a room or a sheet that would raise a new diagnostic is left as it was, with the reason in `unresolved`.

only.description: Run only this stage. Default: `furnish`, then `sheet`.

reissue.description: Allow `paper` and `scale` to be replaced when the drawing does not fit the authored sheet.

tools.name: suggest
tools.description: Suggest the doors and windows a plan's room graph needs, as data; nothing is applied. For a room with no path back, a building with no entrance, a bath reachable only through a bedroom, or a windowless bedroom, it returns ready-to-paste `door`/`window` statements with a rationale, for you to choose among and insert. Each names its wall by an authored id or a unique wall category, else by absolute `at (x, y)` coordinates. Door candidates avoid furniture in the door's approach; window candidates do not consider furniture.

tools.name: complete
tools.description: List the completion items in scope at a source byte offset: keywords, element names, ids and enum values, the same items an editor's language server offers. For structured or assisted authoring.

at.description: Source byte offset to complete at.

tools.name: link
tools.description: Make two URLs that show a plan in the browser with nothing to install, for handing to a person. `playground` opens it in the hosted editor, rendered; `embed` draws it alone, for an iframe. The plan travels inside the URL, after the `#`, so it is never sent to a server and the URL carries nothing else. A plan that does not compile still gets links, and the page shows its diagnostics; `ok` says whether it compiles, and `errors` counts the errors when it does not. `bytes` is the size of the compressed plan in the URL.

instructions:
ArchLang compiles `.arch` text to SVG floor plans. Before writing any `.arch`, read the `archlang://spec` resource: the whole language (from a shell: `npx -y @chanmeng666/archlang spec`).
The loop:
1. Write the plan as `.arch` source.
2. `compile` it. Errors are diagnostics, usually with a byte span, often a fix; `fix` applies the machine-applicable ones, edit the rest by hand.
3. `describe` it; check rooms, areas and doors against the brief.
4. `validate` with strict:true (parse, resolve, `lint`); fix every warning, then back to 2.
5. `finish` once lint is clean, before export: it furnishes empty rectangular rooms (single-storey plans) and adds the missing sheet statements (paper, scale, dimensions, title, room schedule, legend).
With a shell, the CLI runs the same loop at no context cost: `archlang <cmd>`, or `npx -y @chanmeng666/archlang <cmd>` without a global install.
